findings.title: Preserve indirect sharing when remapping class arrays
findings.impact: RenameClasses caches cloned arrays but returns PdfArray values inline into every owner and child slot. The serializer recursively emits every inline occurrence, so compact acyclic indirect class graphs below the depth guard can produce exponential output; valid flat class arrays shared by many elements also multiply output unnecessarily.
evidence: line 76 replaces every /C with RenameClasses return value
lines 89-95 return cached/cloned resolved PdfArray instead of retaining indirect reference representation
PdfPageExtractor.Serialization.cs:367-374 recursively emits inline arrays per occurrence
PdfMerger.Tagged.cs:51-61 serializes the remapped graph without an output byte bound
The new shared-array test uses two owners and validates names/content but does not check retained indirection or amplification.
findings.reachable_example: An accepted /C indirect array DAG in which each array contains two references to the next needs only O(depth) source objects but emits O(2^depth) direct elements after remapping. A flat array of N class names shared by N structure elements emits O(N^2) name tokens. This is source-confirmed; no runtime amplification or crash reproduction was run.
findings.recommendation: Retain/reuse indirect remapped arrays, or reject unsupported nested class syntax before expansion while preserving valid shared flat arrays. Avoid adding a new public limit solely for this path.
findings.disposition: addressed in final uncommitted correction; source-confirmed by the single targeted confirmation below; primary owns full/package/CI proof
